raw_case_text: A 40-year-old male, agriculturist, smoker, nonalcoholic, native of Ravi river valley area (altitude 996 meters above the mean sea level) in Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh, India was admitted in September 2014 with history of fever for 1 month. Fever was high grade recorded up to 105 F and associated with chills without rigors. The patient had history of malaise and easy fatigability for last 3 weeks. Review of other systems was normal. He had no significant past history. Treatment records revealed that he received a course of antibiotic from his primary care physicians without any relief. He denied ever visiting any endemic area of VL. On examination, pallor was present and he was febrile. No icterus and lymphadenopathy were present. His body mass index was 21. Per abdomen examination revealed massive splenomegaly (palpable 8 cm below the left costal margin) and hepatomegaly (liver span 16 cm). Rest of the examination was normal. On hematological investigations, pancytopenia was observed. Hemoglobin was 6.7 g%, leukocyte count was 600 mm3 (neutrophils-41%, lymphocytes-42%, and monocytes-14%), platelet count was 36,000 mm3, and corrected reticulocyte count was 1.2%. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 102 mm/h. Peripheral smear showed macrocytic normochromic picture and was negative for malaria parasite. The results of serial hemogram and biochemistry are shown in Table 1. A prothrombin time of 16 s was recorded (international normalized ratio 1.34), with a normal activated partial thromboplastin time. Blood glucose and renal function were normal. Hepatitis B surface antigen, anti-hepatitis C virus, and human immunodeficiency virus serology were negative. Chest X-ray was normal. Ultrasound of the abdomen showed hepatosplenomegaly and dilated portal vein (15.3 mm). Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal. Empiric treatment for neutropenic fever was prescribed. Blood and urine culture were sterile. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy were performed. Bone marrow morphology was normocellular with normoblastic erythropoiesis. M:E ratio was 1.5:1. Myeloid and megakaryocytic series were normal in maturation and morphology. There was a marked increase in histiocytes with a prominent hemophagocytosis. Amastigote forms of Leishmania donovani were seen both intracellularly and extracellularly [Figure 1]. Serum ferritin was significantly raised (18,500 ng/ml) and triglycerides were 274 mg/dl. The diagnosis of HLH was established as 6 out of 8 diagnostic criteria (5 out of 8 are required) were fulfilled; fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, and hemophagocytosis in the bone marrow. The final diagnosis of VL with secondary hemophagocytic syndrome was made. The patient was started with amphotericin B 1 mg/kg on alternate days and given 15 infusions. The patient became afebrile after the first dose of amphotericin B. At discharge, spleen tip was just palpable and liver span was normal. Hematological and biochemical parameters at discharge are shown in Table 1. The patient remained asymptomatic at the end of 3 months and 6 months during follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old male presented with high-grade fever up to 105 °F for 1 month, accompanied by malaise and fatigability.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 40-year-old male agriculturist presented in September 2014 with a 1-month history of high-grade fever recorded up to 105 °F associated with chills without rigors, and 3 weeks of malaise and easy fatigability. He received an empirical course of antibiotics from primary care physicians without relief. He denied travel to known endemic areas for visceral leishmaniasis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Smoker, non-alcoholic. Agriculturist residing in the Ravi river valley (altitude 996 m), Chamba district, Himachal Pradesh, India. Denied travel to known endemic visceral leishmaniasis zones. Prior empirical antibiotic therapy without improvement. No other past medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: High-grade fever up to 105 °F, chills, malaise, easy fatigability. Denied rigors, cough, dysuria, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or bleeding manifestations.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile, marked pallor; anicteric; no peripheral lymphadenopathy. Body mass index: 21 kg/m^2. Abdominal examination revealed massive splenomegaly palpable 8 cm below the left costal margin and hepatomegaly with a liver span of 16 cm. Remainder of examination was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Severe pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.7 g/dL, leukocyte count 600/mm^3 (neutrophils 41%, lymphocytes 42%, monocytes 14%), platelet count 36,000/mm^3, corrected reticulocyte count 1.2%. ESR: 102 mm/h. Peripheral blood smear: macrocytic normochromic erythrocytes, negative for malaria parasites. Prothrombin time: 16 s (INR 1.34), normal aPTT. Fasting blood glucose, renal function tests normal. Serum ferritin markedly elevated at 18,500 ng/mL; serum triglycerides elevated at 274 mg/dL. Sterile blood and urine cultures. Serologies negative for HBsAg, anti-HCV, and HIV. Chest X-ray normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasonography showed marked hepatosplenomegaly and dilated portal vein (15.3 mm). Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal without varices. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy: normocellular marrow with normoblastic erythropoiesis (M:E ratio 1.5:1), normal myeloid/megakaryocytic maturation, marked increase in histiocytes with prominent hemophagocytosis, and intracellular and extracellular microorganisms.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
Diagnostic Confirmation: Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy demonstrated intracellular and extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania donovani. Fulfilled 6 of 8 HLH diagnostic criteria: fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias (Hb 6.7 g/dL, WBC 600/mm^3, platelets 36,000/mm^3), hyperferritinemia (18,500 ng/mL), hypertriglyceridemia (274 mg/dL), and hemophagocytosis in bone marrow.
Differentials Ruled Out: Malaria (negative smear), viral hepatitis B/C, HIV, enteric fever / bacterial sepsis (sterile blood and urine cultures), and cirrhosis/portal hypertension (normal endoscopy).
Treatment & Clinical Course: Empiric treatment for neutropenic fever was prescribed initially. Specific therapy with intravenous amphotericin B deoxycholate (1 mg/kg on alternate days for 15 infusions) was initiated. The patient defervesced following the first infusion. At discharge, the spleen tip was barely palpable, liver span normalized, and cytopenias and biochemical derangements resolved. The patient remained completely asymptomatic at 3- and 6-month follow-up.
